name: Market Stalls
desc: A row of night-market stalls across the mid-ground — pole frames, trestle counters heaped with crates and produce trays, hand-daubed signboards — under striped canvas awnings that belly and luff on the wind, while a slung festoon of bulbs sways over the row and lays its warm light along the cloth and a food stall breathes steam into the beam.

energy.doc: wind in the awnings, festoon swing, bulb glow and steam

scale.doc: stall height vs frame — stall width and counter follow it

density.doc: how many stalls in the row (2-5), plus crates, trays, bulbs and steam

wear.doc: trodden ground, spilt straw and grime worked under the stalls

speed.doc: wind, festoon swing and steam rate

hue.doc: awning / warm-light hue (28 = ochre canvas; poles and frame always answer cold on the complement)

x.doc: centre of the row as a canvas fraction

y.doc: ground line the stalls stand on — the row builds upward from here

alpha.doc: opacity of cloth, bulbs and steam — drop it to sit the row back in the haze

style.doc: canvas: striped ochre market canvas, modelled cloth with real fold shadow, warm bulbs · tarp: a modern informal pitch — blue polytarp, flat and hard, cold and unlovely · lantern: paper lanterns and pale silk instead of canvas, ribbed and softly backlit · riso: two-ink misregistered print — flat offset duotone, no modelling anywhere · nocturne: form from bulb light only — local colour gone, near-monochrome, the row emerging from the dark exactly as far as the festoon reaches

act.doc: trade: the market is open and working · gust: weather coming — the cloth snaps and the festoon swings hard · shutter: closing up — the wind drops, the steam dies and most of the bulbs are already out

seed.doc: deterministic seed for stall depths, awning cut, signage, which pitch cooks and which bulbs are dead
